assign.request: modify the classdoc system to be a general "Doc" system for classes and non classes alike; make a skill "documentation" invoked before finishing any task; spawn many Sonnet minions to audit every framework/* directory and test the new skill; create framework/audit/ with a readme.md and page.js report; implement the highest-priority fixes; consider how to condense the module set. work autonomously.
assign.now: scoping — reading ext/classdoc, Page, tabs, catalog
steps: Build ext/doc — Doc extends Page, generalized
Fan out one Sonnet agent per framework module
Organization analysis — where the module set condenses
Land — link everything, refresh the skill

assign.now: ext/doc landed; writing the fan-out briefs

log.msg: ext/classdoc → ext/doc. `Doc extends Page` — a class, so a module with a different shape overrides sections()/bar()/well()/member_page() instead of the config growing an option. `Class:` → `subject:`, which may now be a class, a function with properties, a namespace object, or nothing. All 6 call sites migrated; ext/classdoc deleted; every prose reference renamed outside framework/ai (that log records what existed that day).

Two additions Mike asked for mid-flight. (1) A Files tab: ext/files grew an `about` hook, so the module's tree sits beside doc/file/<path>.md sits beside the fetched source — a pseudo-IDE per module. The list is DECLARED, not crawled: directory.json is gitignored, so a crawler-driven tab would be blank in production and nobody who could fix it would ever see it break (ext/doc/doc/files.md). (2) A filename label on code blocks — `code.js(src, "/app.js")` and the markdown fence info string ```js /app.js, one data-file attribute, one rule in highlight.css.

Verified with playwright at 1600: /framework/ext/doc/ shows Overview·API·Docs·Files, and View/Page/App/Router/Sidebar/Socket all render with no console errors. Page keeps its eight tabs (declared children still land between Overview and API).

assign.now: 20 Sonnet auditors running, one per module; 8 queued behind the concurrency cap

log.msg: Fan-out dispatched. One Sonnet agent per module, each pointed at a shared brief (ai/2026-08-15/doc-system/brief.md) rather than 28 copies of it. Fences: an agent may write only readme.md, doc/**/*.md and page.js inside its own directory, plus one audit file at framework/audit/modules/<slug>.md. No .js that is not a page.js, no .css, nothing outside its dir — behaviour changes come back as ranked recommendations, not commits.

Window check before the second half: session 14% → 35% on the first 20 spawns. Target is 50%, ceiling 75% — the remaining 8 audits fit, but the IMPLEMENTATION wave after them will have to be the top findings only, not everything every agent asked for.

agent.outcome: Best-documented module already; the gap was a missing Files tab (no files:, zero doc/file/*.md) plus six stale framework/page.js:N line citations. Fixed both. Top recs: a 14-line JSDoc header in Sidebar.js duplicating the readme (a CLAUDE.md comments-near-zero violation), three $-handles assigned and never read, nested groups rendering href=undefined.

log.msg: First skill fix from agent feedback, applied immediately so the 27 still running get it: the skill did not say whether readme.md itself gets a doc/file/readme.md.md. It does — and core/Page's own audit had already logged that exact miss as its Improvement #1, meaning a previous pass rediscovered it the hard way. A rule two independent readers guessed wrong is a hole in the skill, not in the readers.

assign.now: collecting audits; window at 70% so the implementation wave is off

log.msg: DECISION — no implementation wave. Mike's instruction was to implement the top fixes 'depending on the current token usage window'. The window answered: session 14% → 70% on 28 audits, against a 75% ceiling. So every code recommendation stays a ranked, written finding. Two exceptions, both bugs the audit found in code I wrote TODAY and both one line: ext/files' no-highlight fallback never checked resp.ok (a missing file rendered the SPA fallback's index.html as the file's contents), and ext/doc's patched() banner false-positived on every non-class subject (md.file.name is "" natively, which is the exact signal patched() reads as 'an ext replaced this').

Converging skill feedback, applied mid-flight so later agents got it: (1) does readme.md get its own doc/file/readme.md.md — three agents guessed, two ways; now stated, and the worked example was fixed to match; (2) the Improvements heading is never omitted, even when empty, because an absent section reads as 'not looked at'; (3) NEVER hand-cite a line number — core/Router found ~30 drifted, core/App ~20, core/Page 9 of 13 spot-checked wrong including one claiming 8 callers where the live file has zero; (4) a module with two classes overrides api() and calls members(subject, {prefix}), which is what Doc being a class is for.

ext/tabs' auditor caught a gap in my own migration: the classdoc→doc rename pass ran with --include=*.js --include=*.md, so four CSS comments still named the deleted module. Renamed. The lesson is the audit's in miniature — a rename is only as complete as the glob you ran it with, and nothing fails when a comment lies.

assign.now: audit report built and linked; window reset, so the implementation wave is back on once the last agents land

links.label: Priorities — what to fix, in order

log.msg: The 5h window RESET (live read: 0%, next reset 19:09). The earlier no-implementation call was correct for the window it was made in and is now reversed — the top fixes get implemented once the last agents land. Recording both halves because the reasoning matters more than the verdict: the rule was 'depending on the window', and the window answered differently twice in one session.

framework/audit/ is live: an AuditDoc extends Doc whose docs() override retitles each slug (core-Page → core/Page), one report per module in the left rail, the synthesis in the Overview. Dogfoods the extension point the whole task was about — the retitling is 6 lines in a subclass, not an option on Doc.

Regression found by eye in the sidebar screenshot, not by any test: converting a TOP-LEVEL section page (styles/, ui/) to a Doc leaks its Overview/API/Docs/Files tabs into the framework sidebar, because framework/page.js's sections() enumerates a section's children as sub-entries. `leaf: true` is the existing opt-out (audit/page.js already carries it). Needs adding to styles/page.js and ui/page.js once their agents finish — and it belongs in the skill, since it only bites a page that is BOTH a Doc and a nav section.

26 of 29 audits in. The framework went from 215 doc/*.md files to 701 — roughly 486 new, one per method, property, note and FILE. Nine holes in the documentation skill were found by the agents using it and folded back the same day; the convergences are the signal worth keeping: three agents independently hit the same patched() false-positive, two independently counted the same four duplicated sticky-rail implementations, three converged on the same base-class-plus-subclass workaround before the skill had an answer for it.

assign.now: fix wave: 4 agents on the real bugs, 3 audits still landing

log.msg: Fix wave scope is written down at ai/2026-08-15/doc-system/fixes.md: REAL BUGS ONLY. Every deletion, dedup and rename the audit found is well-argued and none is obviously correct, so they stay recommendations — CLAUDE.md's rule is that a sunk edit presents an unsettled direction as decided and then argues for itself. Committing ext/Panel and ext/editor is the highest-risk finding and is explicitly NOT done: commit only when asked.

ext/Ask's audit surfaced the one finding worth Mike's eye that is not a doc problem and not a crash: its two PRODUCTION chat surfaces (dev rail, task chat) pass no tools restriction at all, while start() in the same module deliberately floors itself at acceptEdits. The deliberate path is the restricted one; the two paths used daily are not. Bounded — the bridge is localhost-only by construction — but it reads as an oversight rather than a decision. Recorded as §0.5 on Priorities with call sites; NOT changed, because which way it should go is Mike's call.

agent.outcome: destroy() now cancels first — one line. Verified the real way: Playwright grabbed a handle, moved (ghost+placeholder live, pointer captured), called destroy() mid-gesture, then asserted ghost/placeholder count 0/0 and dragging false. Idle destroy still a no-op, double destroy doesn't throw, and a full drag still reorders.

instantiate() now try/catches and resolves ready() unconditionally — the failure is visible in the console AND on screen, and app.ready always settles. The telling part: a 10-line edit invalidated ~20 line citations in the module's own docs, which the agent then had to repair. The citation-rot finding demonstrating itself inside the fix for a different bug.

19 components, 3 exported functions and 16 copy-paste templates — the asymmetry is the module. Found a real trap in ext/doc: content() runs bound to the OVERVIEW SECTION, not the Doc, so this.previews() inside it silently draws nothing. Documented in ext/doc's Traps; whether the binding should change is now Open. Also judged, correctly, that the 19 leaf demo pages should NOT become Docs — they are already the demo system.

log.msg: The strongest single piece of evidence for the line-citation rule arrived inside an unrelated fix: core/App's agent changed 10 lines and thereby invalidated ~20 file:line citations in that module's own docs, which it then had to hunt down and repair. Nothing warned. That is the rot happening in real time, in a session that had already banned the practice.

agent.outcome: drain() now try/catch/finally so writing always clears — a failed write costs one save, not every save after it. FileSaver.load() rejects on non-404 instead of folding every failure into null, so null means genuinely absent; workspace() catches and refuses to seed. Also opened its own task dir mid-work after noticing it had skipped new-task.

Factored the two disagreeing end-time computations into one end(it, start) used by both — the defect was the duplication, the overlap was the symptom. Added a demo that would catch a regression. Found a NEW bug on the way: unnamed POJO children in an overview: array all key as undefined in Page.declare(), so only the last renders.

Removed the unconditional changed() call whose only job was giving the badge a value; its side effect was a save on every visit. Verified by mtime before/after a load, then a real edit to prove saving still works, then cleaned the test artifact back to byte-identical.

log.msg: A fix wave found a bug the audit wave missed: ext/Timeline's agent hit Page.declare() keying every unnamed POJO child as `undefined`, so only the LAST survives — silently. It matters because ext/doc's `overview:` array is exactly that shape, which means the new documentation system has been quietly eating demo cards all day. Dispatched as its own fix, with the proof being Timeline's own two-card rail.

agent.outcome: One .catch() with the page's log_label. The diagnosis beat the audit's: on COLD BOOT the rejection reached App.instantiate()'s catch and wiped the whole $pages tree into an error screen; on later navigation Router.load() never re-awaits loaders, so it became an unhandled rejection with no attribution. Two different failures, one missing catch. Proved with a throwing scratch page, then deleted the scratch.

log.msg: Sidebar regression closed: ui/page.js is a Doc AND a top-level nav section, so it needed leaf: true or its Overview/API/Docs/Files tabs render as sidebar entries. styles/ did not need it — its auditor attempted the six hub conversions, read Doc.js and tabs.js, realised a hub with real children: would mount permanent tab chrome across up to ~90 descendant urls, and REVERTED rather than ship an unverifiable structural change. That reversal is the best judgment call any agent made today, and it is direct evidence that the five-block demo system and the Doc system are a load-bearing boundary rather than a historical accident.

agent.outcome: declare() now derives an unnamed POJO child's key with Page.slug(child.title), mirroring the array-pair branch one line below; a duplicate derived name warns rather than silently swallowing. Proof: ext/Timeline's Overview rail went from ['Overview','Windows & nested children'] to ['Overview','Orientation & lanes','Windows & nested children'].

log.msg: The final crawl earned its keep. 39 module pages at 1600: three failed, and TWO were the trap I had documented in ext/doc's readme an hour earlier — ext/LayoutTool and ext/Ask both threw on this.look()/this.asker(), helpers they had written on the Doc config one line above the call. Plus ui's auditor, who lost time to the same thing silently. Three independent readers expecting `this` to be the Doc is the design telling you which binding is right, so overview_section() now binds content to the Doc and the trap became a fix. The third failure is a deliberate md.file("does-not-exist.md") demo showing the Not-written-yet state live — a false positive in my crawler, and exactly the show-dont-tell the skill asks for.
Final sweep: 38/39 pages clean, the 39th clean by design. No console errors, no horizontal overflow, no unintended md-error boxes.

assign.outcome:
**ext/classdoc became ext/doc, and every framework module was audited by its own agent.** /framework/audit/ · /framework/audit/overview/priorities/ · /framework/audit/overview/organization/ · /framework/ext/doc/

Doc extends Page — a class, so a module with a different shape OVERRIDES (sections, api, members, bar, well, docs) instead of the config growing an option. `subject:` now takes a class, a function with properties, a namespace object (`import * as X` is the safe spelling), or nothing. New Files tab: ext/files grew an `about` hook, so each module's tree sits beside doc/file/<path>.md sits beside the fetched source. New filename labels on code blocks, one data-file attribute with two emitters.

29 Sonnet agents audited every module against a new `documentation` skill that was itself the subject of the test. The framework went from 215 doc/*.md to 766, including 298 doc/file/*.md — a category that did not exist that morning — and from 6 Doc pages to 40.

Ten holes in the skill were found by the agents using it and folded back the same day. The convergences are the signal: three agents independently hit the same patched() false-positive, two independently counted the same four duplicated sticky-rail implementations, three converged on the same base-class workaround, and three expected content() to be bound to the Doc — which is why it now is.

8 real bugs fixed, each proven not asserted (mid-drag destroy asserted at ghost-count 0, mtime unchanged across a page load, a two-card rail that used to render one). Every deletion, dedup and rename stays a RANKED RECOMMENDATION: none is obviously correct, and a sunk edit presents an unsettled direction as decided.

⚠ TWO THINGS NEED MIKE. (1) ext/Panel and ext/editor have NO git history — 972 lines in the working tree only; committing is not mine to do unasked. (2) ext/Ask's two production chat surfaces pass no tools restriction while start() in the same module floors itself at acceptEdits.

Final sweep: 38/39 module pages clean at 1600, the 39th clean by design.

log.msg: landed — ext/doc replaces classdoc as an extendable class, a documentation skill now gates every task, and 29 agents audited every framework module into /framework/audit/
